name: re
method: Claude Sonnet 5.5 read the public Kaggle profile page and the public Competitions page with the Claude desktop app's built-in browser pane (the one existing tab, no other browser) on 2026-10-30, waiting about six seconds after each load and five seconds between the two pages. Page text was read, the medal icons were read from the page (alt text on each medal image, cross-checked against a screenshot of the list), the teammate accounts shown beside each entry were read from the hover titles on the small avatars, the join date was read from the 'Joined' tooltip, and the avatar image address was read from the profile picture element. No rate limit, captcha or block appeared. No earlier draft file existed for this person, so nothing was carried over; the repo record's own claims are listed under unverified where they were not re-read.

teamNotes: The Kaggle Competitions page does not show team names, only the accounts beside each entry, so teamName is null on every row. Three of the five medals are team entries: Nemotron gold (goodmeatday, refv00, reopon), NeuroGolf gold (stmx35, tomo1314, tknakamu, refv00, schrodinger0112) and RSNA Knee silver (stmx35, tknakamu, ruikikobayashi, refv00); none of these is credited to re alone. The Waveform Inversion silver and the CMI bronze show only the refv00 account, and Kaggle's activity panel counts five solo and five team entries, which matches that reading: the five solo entries are those two plus the Aneurysm and the two Playground rows, and the five team entries are the three completed team rows above plus the two active ARC Prize entries, whose cards show several accounts. Two accounts, stmx35 and tknakamu, appear beside both the NeuroGolf and the RSNA Knee entries. The profile's Featured Writeups shows a 1st Place Solution writeup for the Nemotron challenge dated June 24, 2026, written as 'we' and labelled NullSira beside its date line; Kaggle does not say on that card whether NullSira is a team name, so it is not recorded as one. The repo record's separate ARC Prize 2026 roster observation, a team listed under a Japanese-language name in both ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3, was not re-read today and is not repeated as a Kaggle-page fact.
